description: Auto-normalize skills at insert time, LLM fallback for unknown skills, and incremental normalization endpoint.
steps: Add LLM fallback helper to src/lib/skill-taxonomy.ts that calls GPT-4o-mini to categorize unknown skills, with try/catch and graceful degradation.
Update POST /api/jobs to normalize and categorize each skill at creation time using the taxonomy (and LLM fallback for unknowns).
Update POST /api/experience to normalize and categorize each skill at creation time.
Update PATCH /api/experience/[id] to normalize and categorize skills when they are replaced.
Change POST /api/skills/normalize to only process records where normalizedName is null by default. Add optional force:true body parameter to re-process all.
Verify build passes with npm run build.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/jobs stores skills with normalizedName and category populated at creation time
POST /api/experience stores skills with normalizedName and category populated at creation time
PATCH /api/experience/[id] stores skills with normalizedName and category populated when skills are updated
LLM fallback is called for skills not in static taxonomy, wrapped in try/catch
LLM failure or missing API key gracefully degrades (leaves category as null)
POST /api/skills/normalize only processes null normalizedName records by default
POST /api/skills/normalize with force:true re-processes all records
npm run build completes without errors
verification: npm run build exits with code 0
findings: Build passes cleanly. Added three new exported functions to skill-taxonomy.ts: normalizeAndCategorize (sync), categorizeSkilLWithLLM (async LLM call), and normalizeAndCategorizeWithFallback (combined). All API routes use a two-pass approach: first static taxonomy (fast, sync), then LLM fallback only for unrecognized skills (async, non-blocking). The normalize endpoint now returns a 'mode' field indicating incremental vs full, and a 'llmCategorized' count showing how many were resolved via LLM.
